::: {.justify style="margin: 50px 0;"}

I am contributing to develop metamaterial-based tip-transforming catheters at Nimble Surgical.
Previously, I was a Faculty Research Assistant in the Intelligent Machines and Materials Lab, part of Collaborative Robotics and Intelligent Systems (CoRIS) Institute at Oregon State University.
I developed hardware for integrating flexible sensors for augmenting human-supervised underwater grasping. Prior to this, I built and characterized soft grippers and robot arm,
and 

My work sits at the intersection of mechanical engineering, robotics, materials, and computation to some extent.
I design the system, fabricate it, characterize, then feed what I learned back into the design.

Outside of work, I am a virtual pilot and hobbyist photographer.

Read more about my work on the [research](research.html) page.

    <li class="work__card">
      <b class="work__card-title">High-Payload Soft Robots</b>
      <span class="work__card-detail">Soft robots are safe and adaptable, but their compliant bodies can twist or buckle under load. I used torsion-resistant structures to preserve compliance while carrying useful payloads.</span>
    </li>
    <li class="work__card">
      <b class="work__card-title">Underwater Manipulation</b>
      <span class="work__card-detail">Operators lose reliable visual feedback in turbulent, low-visibility conditions at depth. I integrated flexible tactile sensors onto existing hardware to help assess grasp stability.</span>
    </li>
    <li class="work__card">
      <b class="work__card-title">Agricultural Robots</b>
      <span class="work__card-detail">Soft fruit picking is a narrow force-control problem: too much damages the fruit, and too little lets it slip. I built sensorized grippers that generate useful grasp data to teach robots.</span>
    </li>
